## Factual research brief

### 1. Expression passed to `getInstance(...)`

| Expression | Declaring type from supplied imports | Runtime value |
|---|---|---|
| `TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm()` | `javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory` | **Not a compile-time literal and not determinable exactly from the supplied imports/source identifier alone.** The method returns the current Java security-property value of `ssl.TrustManagerFactory.algorithm`; the property may be changed at runtime. If that property is absent, the result is implementation-specific. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/javax/net/ssl/TrustManagerFactory.html)) |

For the Oracle/OpenJDK JSSE reference implementation, the documented default value of `ssl.TrustManagerFactory.algorithm` is **`"PKIX"`**. Thus, on an unmodified Oracle/OpenJDK JSSE configuration, the expression evaluates to `PKIX`. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/27/security/java-secure-socket-extension-jsse-reference-guide.html))

`PKIX` is also the Java-platform-required standard `TrustManagerFactory` algorithm name. However, that requirement means Java SE implementations must support `PKIX`; it does **not** make `getDefaultAlgorithm()` universally or immutably return `PKIX`, because the API explicitly permits the default to be selected by the security property. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/docs/api/java.base/javax/net/ssl/TrustManagerFactory.html))

**Source limitation:** the supplied material does not state the target runtime (for example, a particular JDK distribution/version, Android API level, configured security-property file, or any runtime calls to `Security.setProperty`). Therefore the only exact environment-independent answer is: the property’s current value, or an implementation-specific fallback if absent. The documented Oracle/OpenJDK default is `PKIX`.

### 2. External interoperability specification

`org.cryptomator.data.cloud.webdav.network.DefaultTrustManager`, `tryToFindDefaultTrustManager`, and the detector text about `TrustManagerFactory.init(null)` do **not** themselves identify a published wire protocol, file format, remote-service API, or RFC that mandates a particular value for this `TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(...)` parameter.

The governed parameter is a **Java/JSSE trust-manager-factory algorithm name**, selected through the Java security-provider mechanism. `PKIX` is a Java Security Standard Algorithm Name, describing a factory that performs X.509 certification-path validation according to the IETF PKIX rules (RFC 5280 or a successor), but no supplied finding identifier establishes that the application must select `PKIX` rather than honor the configured platform default. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/specs/security/standard-names.html?utm_source=openai))
